loop.top3_why: The mean of the full pool (family mean) provides a simple, robust aggregation that is stable across all three validation windows (0.65–0.71). It avoids the high variance and over‑fitting risk seen in the weighted inverse‑error strategy (A), whose per‑window error spikes to 0.85. The mean strategy also aligns with the dataset prior, where plain mean is among the top performers, and it matches the diagnosis that a robust combination is preferable when model rankings are unstable.
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate A, while having the lowest validation score, shows a large outlier in the third window (0.85), indicating over‑fitting to the validation set and high sensitivity to the limited number of windows. Candidate C (dba) has a slightly higher score than B and similar per‑window stability, but the DTW barycenter is more computationally intensive and offers no clear advantage over the simple mean in this context. Therefore, B is the safest choice for generalization.
